v1.feedback: The skitter mechanic itself is well-implemented — per-particle jitter directions, staccato phase, and the chartreuse iridescence flash genuinely sell the 'startled insects' concept. But the underlying form is just five concentric spherical shells; the silhouette reads as a generic particle orb regardless of skitter state. A refined version should break the spherical symmetry — distribute particles along a recognizable armature (branching coral, a cluster of pod shapes, even a flattened disc colony) so the skitter has a legible resting state to depart from and return to. The palette swerve from parent is present but mild; lean harder into the chartreuse as a persistent accent rather than a transient flash.

v2.feedback: The skitter mechanic genuinely earns its name — phase-offset staccato scatter with per-particle jitter reads as insect-swarm startle, not generic noise. Coral armature is biomorphic and vertical, palette swerve from amber to chartreuse is a real departure from the parent's drift. Two issues to fix: (1) the piece lives or dies on mic input — without audio the coral just breathes faintly, so add a slow autonomous skitter pulse (e.g. periodic Poisson-timed bursts) as a fallback so the form is alive even with no mic granted; (2) additive blending on 20k particles at the dense inner trunk will wash to white — multiply alpha by an inverse-density term or cap shell-0 alpha harder so the silhouette stays readable instead of blooming into a glow pillar.
